reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive peroxisome biogenesis disorder caused by variants in one of many PEX genes, most often PEX1
It is the most severe end of the Zellweger spectrum, which also includes neonatal adrenoleukodystrophy and infantile Refsum disease
Failure of peroxisome assembly impairs multiple peroxisomal functions, including very-long-chain fatty acid beta-oxidation and plasmalogen synthesis
The biochemical signature is raised plasma very-long-chain fatty acids, with low plasmalogens and abnormal bile acid intermediates
Neonates present with profound hypotonia, poor feeding, seizures, a characteristic dysmorphic facies and a large fontanelle
Hepatic dysfunction, renal cortical cysts and chondrodysplasia punctata (stippled epiphyses) are supporting features
Sensorineural deafness and retinal and other ocular abnormalities are common
There is no curative treatment; management is supportive and the classic form is usually fatal in infancy
reference.pathophysiology: Peroxisomes are organelles that carry out several essential metabolic reactions, including the beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids, synthesis of ether phospholipids (plasmalogens) and bile acids, and detoxification of hydrogen peroxide. PEX genes encode peroxins required to assemble the peroxisomal membrane and import matrix enzymes. In Zellweger syndrome, defective peroxins prevent normal peroxisome assembly, so matrix enzymes are not imported and are degraded, leaving functionally empty or absent peroxisomes. The resulting accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids and deficiency of plasmalogens disrupt membrane and myelin integrity and neuronal migration, producing the severe multisystem, and particularly neurological, phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Other neonatal hypotonia and encephalopathy syndromes
Single peroxisomal enzyme defects (for example X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, D-bifunctional protein deficiency)
Congenital muscular dystrophies and congenital myopathies
Chromosomal and other multiple congenital anomaly syndromes
Neonatal metabolic encephalopathies of other causes
additionalInvestigations: Plasma very-long-chain fatty acid profile (raised) as the key screening test
Erythrocyte plasmalogen levels (reduced) and plasma bile acid intermediates
Molecular genetic testing of the PEX genes
Neuroimaging assessing neuronal migration defects and white matter change
Renal ultrasound for cortical cysts and skeletal imaging for stippled epiphyses
Hearing and ophthalmological assessment and liver function tests
redFlags: Profound neonatal hypotonia with seizures and poor feeding
Dysmorphic facies with a large fontanelle and hepatic dysfunction
Progressive deterioration with apnoea and failure to thrive
Coagulopathy or bleeding from hepatic involvement
reference.prognosis: The classic Zellweger phenotype carries a very poor prognosis, with most affected infants dying within the first year of life. Milder disorders within the Zellweger spectrum have longer survival with progressive neurological, hepatic, visual and hearing impairment.
pitfalls: Attributing severe neonatal hypotonia to a neuromuscular disorder without checking peroxisomal biochemistry
Missing the diagnosis by not requesting very-long-chain fatty acids
Overlooking associated hearing and visual impairment that affect management
Failing to recognise milder Zellweger spectrum phenotypes presenting later
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Provide supportive and palliative care as the mainstay, since no treatment corrects the peroxisome-biogenesis defect
Support nutrition with assisted or gastrostomy feeding for poor feeding and hypotonia, and supplement the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K
Consider bile acid supplementation with cholic acid for the abnormal bile acid intermediates and hepatic dysfunction, giving vitamin K to correct coagulopathy
Manage sensory impairment with hearing aids for deafness and cataract or ophthalmological surgery for visual involvement
Monitor hepatic function, growth and neurological status with regular review
Offer genetic counselling and PEX-gene testing for this autosomal recessive disorder, with carrier testing and prenatal and reproductive options
Coordinate multidisciplinary care with early involvement of palliative services given the very poor prognosis
